DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph s. 2021 OPINION NO. SEP 26 HON. LORELIE GERONIMO PACQUIAO Mayor General Santos City Hall 57+5MH, cuty Hall Dr General Santos City Dear Mayor Pacquiao: This has reference to your letter dated June 19, 2023 requesting for legal opinion on the following: 1. WHETHER OR NOT THE CITY MAYOR HAS THE AUTHORITY TO HIRE JOB ORDER WORKERS AND SIGN JOB ORDER CONTRACTS; and 2. WHETHER OR NOT THE DETERMINATION OF 2/3 VOTE TO OVERRIDE A VETO INCLUDES THE CITY VICE MAYOR. The facts surrounding the herein request are as follows: • • • On May 9, 2023, the Sangguniang Panlungsod (SP) of General Santos City passed and approved Appropriation Ordinance NO. 05, series of 2023. On May 23, 2023, the SP transmitted a copy of the Appropriation Ordinance to the City Mayor's Office for the Mayor's approval. Having noted that the Maintenance and Other Operating Expenses (MOOE) - Other Professional Services and Other General Services under the Office of the Vice Mayor, Secretary, are intended for the wages of Job Orders (JOS), the Mayor Pacquiao delivered her Item Veto Message to the SP dated May 29, 2023 on the grounds that the above-mentioned are ultra vires, given that the appropriated amounts are for the wages of JOS. Mayor Pacquiao's contention is that hiring of JOS solely belongs to the Mayor. Nevertheless, on June 6, 2023, the SP consisting of sixteen (16) members including the Vice Mayor, passed Resolution No. 840, series of 2023 overriding the veto with only ten (IO) votes favoring the override and three (3) against the override and one (I) abstained. Hence, the herein requests. "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

The first issue stemmed from the seemingly conflicting views between the view of the Department and of the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) on who has the power between the Mayor and Vice Mayor to hire COS and JOS. In this regard, we would like to inform you that we have already sought further clarification from the Department of Budget and Management and Commission on Audit on this matter. As to the second issue, you contended that the law requires 2/3 vote of all members of the SP, then the 2/3 votes required to override a veto in the present setup composition of the SP of General Santos City is equivalent to 10.67 (16x2/3) or 11 votes. It cannot be IO votes this is short of the required 2/3 votes of ALL member. On a note, the Vice Mayor is included in the 16 membership. Mayor Pacquiao also represented that the standard set by the SP is as follows: Matter to vote Quorum Override of Veto Re uired Majority 2/3 Base er SP All members, including Vice Ma or All members, excluding Vice Mayor or all voting members Base er Law All members of the San unian All members of the Sanggunian This standard set by the SP we believe is contained in their Internal Rules of Procedure (IRP). Thus, this level perused Republic Act No. 5412 or the "Charter of the City of General Santos", which was enacted on June 15, 1968. Section 15 thereof made no mention on the 2/3 votes, pertinently, it provides: xxx A majority of all the members of the city council shall constitute a quorum for the transaction of business, but a smaller number may adjourn from day to day and may compel the immediate attendance of any member who is absent without good cause by issuing to the police of the city an order for his arrest and production to the session under such penalties as shall have been previously prescribed by ordinance. The affirmative vote of a majority of all the members shall be necessary for the passage of any ordinance or of any resolution or motion directing the payment of money or creating liability, but other measures shall prevail upon the majority votes of the members present at any session duly called and held. The ayes and nays shall be taken and recorded upon the passage of all ordinances, upon all resolutions or motions directing the payment of money or creating liability, and at the request of any member, upon any other resolution or motion. Each approved ordinance, resolution or motion shall be sealed with the seal of the City Council and recorded in a book kept for the purpose and shall, on the day following its passage be posted by the secretary at the main entrance of the city hall and in at least two other public places, and shall take effect and be in force on and after the tenth day following its passage unless othemise stated in said ordinance, resolution or motion, or vetoed by the mayor as hereinafter provided. A vetoed ordinance, if repassed, shall take effect ten days after the veto is overridden Page 2 of 4

by the required votes unless otherwise stated in the ordinance, resolution or motion, or again disapproved by the mayor within the said time. (Emphasis supplied) xxx On October 10, 1991 , the Local Government Code of 1991 (LGC) was enacted. Thus, the provision as provided in the LGC should prevail regarding the overriding a veto. Sections 49 and 54 thereof states: Section 49. Presiding Officer. - (a) The vice-governor shall be the presiding officer of the sangguniang panlalawigan; the city vice-mayor, of the sangguniang panlungsod; the municipal vice-mayor, of the sangguniang bayan; and the punong barangay, of the sangguniang barangay. The presiding officer shall vote only to break a tie. (b) In the event of the inability of the regular presiding officer to preside at a sanggunian session, the members present and constituting a quorum shall elect from among themselves a temporary presiding officer. He shall certify within ten (IO) days from the passage of ordinances enacted and resolutions adopted by the sanggunian in the session over which he temporarily presided. Section 54. Approval of Ordinances. - (a) Every ordinance enacted by the sangguniang panlalawigan, sangguniang panlungsod, or sangguniang bayan shall be presented to the provincial governor or city or municipal mayor, as the case may be. If the local chief executive concerned approves the same, he shall affix his signature on each and every page thereof; otherwise, he shall veto it and return the same with his objections to the sanggunian, which may proceed to reconsider the same. The sanggunian concerned may override the veto of the local chief executive by two-thirds (2/3) vote of all its members, thereby making the ordinance or resolution effective for all legal intents and purposes. Xxx (Emphasis ours) Based on the foregoing, a 2/3/ vote of all SP members is required for the overriding of the veto by the City Mayor. Since the City Vice-Mayor is also a member of the SP, as such, he is included in the determination of quorum, it is our view that the total membership of the SP, that is sixteen (16) shall be the basis in the computation of the 2/3 votes. This is the proper interpretation on the phrase "two-thirds (2/3) vote of all its members"l. Hence, a 2/3 vote of 16 members will give us a mathematical result of 10.67. Let it be noted however, that a fraction cannot be considered as one whole vote since it is physically and legally impossible to count or divide a person. Neither can we go down to 10 because definitely, it is less than 2/3 of the Sanggunian membership. Thus, the voting requirement to muster 2/3 votes of all of the sixteen- membership Sanggunian shall be 11 Let it be noted, however, that in the eleven (11) votes required to muster the 2/3 vote, the 11 votes should be coming from the floor, that is, excluding the Presiding Officer, because the latter can vote only to break a tie pursuant to Section 49 of the LGC. 1 DILG Opinion NO. 82, s. 2007 dated September 27, 2007 Page 3 of 4

Foregoing considered, the ten (10) votes mustered by the SP is short of the eleven votes required. Finally, in light of the Supreme Court pronouncement that IRP does not have the force of law but are merely in the nature of by-laws prescribed for the orderly and convenient conduct of proceedings, and that they are merely procedural and not substantive, it is thus clear that the IRP not being a law cannot rise above and be more superior than the express provision of the LGC. Having presented that the IRP of the Sanggunian excluded the Vice Mayor in the computation of 2/3 votes, we recommend to advise the concerned Sanggunian the need to amend that particular Rule in order to conform with the law. This opinion is being rendered based on the facts represented and without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts on the issues herein presented. We hope to have ayou on the matter. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY THORITY OF THE SECRETARY: AT AN CTOR R.
